title: The Almost Yearbook
premise: Mirabel Voss has spent four years at Hollow Creek High perfecting the art of being overlooked, counting down to graduation in a town where everyone knows everyone and no one knows them. When the school's legendary ghost begins leaving notes addressed to Mirabel by name — written in ink that shouldn't exist — they discover the ghost is a former student who died decades ago under circumstances the town buried, and who can only rest if the truth is spoken aloud. To uncover it, Mirabel must win two championships: the academic decathlon that could earn them a scholarship out of town, and the trust of the descendants of those who covered everything up. In the end, Mirabel chooses truth over safety, exposing what happened even though it costs them the scholarship and their closest friendship — but the ghost's release, and Mirabel's own decision to stop hiding, prove that some victories don't come with trophies.
about_author: Marguerite Lockridge grew up in a small river town where the high school yearbook went back further than anyone wanted to admit. She writes stories about kids who refuse to be footnotes.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred People, One Exit
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Senior year begins; we see their careful invisibility, the countdown calendar, and the casual cruelty of small-town life. Emotional beat: weary resignation masking a fierce, unspoken hope for escape.

chapters.title: The Note in Locker 114
chapters.summary: Mirabel finds a note addressed by name: 'You count days. I counted years.' The ink shimmers wrong under light. POV Mirabel. Emotional beat: first crack of fear and thrilling recognition — someone sees them.

chapters.title: What Everyone Knows About Agnes Pike
chapters.summary: Mirabel researches the school ghost legend: Agnes Pike, class of 1974, drowned in the reservoir the night before graduation. Official story: accident. POV Mirabel. Emotional beat: curiosity hardening into suspicion of the town itself.

chapters.title: Decathlon Tryouts
chapters.summary: Mirabel joins the academic decathlon team as their scholarship ticket, clashing with team captain Denny Kowalczyk, golden boy of a founding family. POV Mirabel. Emotional beat: ambition tangled with resentment toward people born to win.

chapters.title: Ink That Isn't Ink
chapters.summary: A chemistry teacher tests the note's ink: no known compound matches, and it predates every pen sold locally. POV alternating Mirabel and Denny, who secretly found a note too. Emotional beat: shared secret forming between enemies.

chapters.title: The Reservoir at Low Water
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Denny visit the drained reservoir and find Agnes's initials carved deep beneath the waterline — carved from inside something. POV Mirabel. Emotional beat: dread giving way to certainty that this was no accident.

chapters.title: Loyalty Has an Address
chapters.summary: Denny learns his grandfather was sheriff the year Agnes died and warns Mirabel to drop it — his family's name is on the scholarship endowment. POV Denny. Emotional beat: loyalty and guilt pulling him apart.

chapters.title: Notes From the Deep End
chapters.summary: The ghost escalates: notes appear in Mirabel's yearbook, filling blank pages with fragments of 1974 — a party, a threat, a scream. POV Mirabel. Emotional beat: grief for a girl the town erased.

chapters.title: The Yearbook Committee
chapters.summary: Mirabel joins yearbook staff to access the archive, discovering pages razored out of the 1974 edition. POV Mirabel. Emotional beat: the thrill of investigation shadowed by how far someone went to hide it.

chapters.title: Denny's Confession, Half of It
chapters.summary: Denny admits his grandfather's journal exists in the family attic but begs Mirabel to wait until after regionals. POV Denny. Emotional beat: friendship tested by inherited shame.

chapters.title: Regional Champions
chapters.summary: The decathlon team wins regionals; Mirabel is briefly, publicly celebrated for the first time. The ghost leaves a note: 'They cheer loud when you're useful.' POV Mirabel. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into clarity.

chapters.title: The Journal
chapters.summary: Denny finally brings the journal: his grandfather wrote that Agnes was pushed after threatening to expose a teacher's abuse of students — including Denny's own father. POV Denny. Emotional beat: horror and the weight of complicity across generations.

chapters.title: Witnesses Still Breathing
chapters.summary: Mirabel tracks down two surviving classmates of Agnes; one denies everything, one whispers 'she asked me to walk her home and I didn't.' POV Mirabel. Emotional beat: the cost of cowardice, then and now.

chapters.title: Threats With Letterheads
chapters.summary: The Kowalczyk family's lawyer threatens Mirabel with defamation and revocation of the decathlon scholarship fund. POV Mirabel. Emotional beat: terror — the choice between future and truth made flesh.

chapters.title: The Friend Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Mirabel's only friend, Priya, reveals she was asked to report on Mirabel's digging — and did, once, before stopping. Trust shatters. POV Priya. Emotional beat: betrayal and the loneliness of being the only out kid with no safe harbor.

chapters.title: State Semifinals, Empty Stomach
chapters.summary: Mirabel competes while the town whispers; Denny, pressured to denounce them, instead refuses on stage. POV alternating. Emotional beat: unexpected solidarity, and stakes rising — lose the final, lose everything.

chapters.title: What Agnes Left in the Walls
chapters.summary: Following the ghost's clues, Mirabel finds Agnes's hidden letter behind the auditorium wall naming her killer — the beloved teacher whose family still runs the school board. POV Mirabel. Emotional beat: cold, certain resolve.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: The team wins the state decathlon; Mirabel stands on stage holding a trophy while knowing the real verdict comes tomorrow. POV Mirabel. Emotional beat: hollow victory, quiet courage gathering.

chapters.title: Graduation Eve, Fifty Years Later
chapters.summary: At the anniversary assembly, Mirabel reads Agnes's letter aloud before the whole town, naming names, refusing to be managed. Chaos, then silence, then old witnesses standing up one by one. POV Mirabel. Emotional beat: the climax — truth spoken at last, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: Consequences
chapters.summary: The scholarship is withdrawn; the teacher's family retaliates; but the state reopens the case and the school renames its library for Agnes. Priya apologizes; forgiveness is offered slowly. POV Priya. Emotional beat: grief and repair beginning.

chapters.title: The Last Note
chapters.summary: On graduation day, a final note appears in Mirabel's cap: 'Thank you for counting me back in.' The ink fades to ordinary black — the ghost is free. POV Mirabel. Emotional beat: release, tenderness, farewell.

chapters.title: The Almost Yearbook
chapters.summary: Mirabel restores the razored 1974 pages and adds their own photo and name beside Agnes's — visible, permanent, unashamed — then boards the bus out of Hollow Creek, not fleeing but leaving whole. POV Mirabel. Emotional beat: identity claimed; the sentence served was never theirs.
